title.en: Professional Communication in a Digital, Social, Mobile World
title.ms: Komunikasi Profesional dalam Dunia Digital, Sosial dan Mudah Alih

en: Explain the importance of effective communication to your career and to the companies where you will work
Explain what it means to communicate as a professional in a business context
Describe the communication process model and how social media are changing business communication
Outline the challenges and opportunities of mobile communication in business
List four general guidelines for using communication technology effectively
Define ethics, distinguish an ethical dilemma from an ethical lapse, and list six guidelines for ethical communication
ms: Terangkan kepentingan komunikasi berkesan kepada kerjaya dan syarikat tempat anda bekerja
Terangkan maksud berkomunikasi secara profesional dalam konteks perniagaan
Huraikan model proses komunikasi dan cara media sosial mengubah komunikasi perniagaan
Gariskan cabaran dan peluang komunikasi mudah alih dalam perniagaan
Senaraikan empat garis panduan umum menggunakan teknologi komunikasi dengan berkesan
Takrif etika, bezakan dilema etika dengan kecuaian etika, dan senaraikan enam garis panduan komunikasi beretika

big.en: Communication skill = the single most important career skill.

groups.en: Why it matters to the company
Figure 1.1: three ways meaning is shared

blocks.en: Employers are often frustrated by poor communication skills, particularly in recent graduates who have not yet learned to adapt their style to a professional business environment. If you write well, speak well, listen well and recognise the appropriate way to communicate in any situation, you gain a major advantage throughout your career.
blocks.ms: Majikan sering kecewa dengan kemahiran komunikasi yang lemah, terutama graduan baharu yang belum belajar menyesuaikan gaya dengan persekitaran perniagaan profesional. Jika anda menulis, bercakap dan mendengar dengan baik serta tahu cara berkomunikasi yang sesuai, anda mendapat kelebihan besar sepanjang kerjaya.

blocks.en: In any role (employee, executive, consultant, freelancer, entrepreneur) you communicate, collaborate and share ideas with people **inside and outside** the organisation. Communication skills may be the **single most important skill** you have.
blocks.ms: Dalam apa-apa peranan (pekerja, eksekutif, perunding, pekerja bebas, usahawan) anda berkomunikasi, bekerjasama dan berkongsi idea dengan orang **dalam dan luar** organisasi. Kemahiran komunikasi mungkin **kemahiran terpenting** anda.

blocks.en: Why it matters to the company
Memory hook: T-C-C-P-M-E (Trust, Community, Clients, Productivity, Marketing, Employees).
blocks.ms: Cara ingat: T-C-C-P-M-E (Trust, Community, Clients, Productivity, Marketing, Employees).

blocks.en: Figure 1.1: three ways meaning is shared

en: Top exchange: the sender’s meaning is transmitted **intact**; the receiver accepts it at face value.
Middle exchange: sender and receiver **negotiate** the meaning by discussing (everything is fine so far, but the risk of schedule slip is higher).
Bottom exchange: the receiver has a **negative emotional reaction** to the word “think” and creates **her own meaning** (things are probably not fine).
ms: Atas: makna penghantar sampai **utuh**; penerima menerimanya seadanya.
Tengah: penghantar dan penerima **merunding** makna melalui perbincangan (setakat ini baik, tetapi risiko lewat jadual lebih tinggi).
Bawah: penerima bertindak balas **negatif secara emosi** pada perkataan “think” dan mencipta **makna sendiri** (mungkin tidak baik).

en: Give **facts** rather than vague impressions — Rather than vague impressions: concrete language, specific detail; support opinions with compelling evidence.
Present information in a **concise, efficient** manner — Concise messages respect people’s time and raise the chance of a positive response.
**Clarify expectations and responsibilities** — Craft messages for a specific response from a specific audience.
Offer **compelling, persuasive** arguments and recommendations — Show readers precisely how they benefit.
ms: Beri **fakta** dan bukan gambaran kabur — Bukan gambaran kabur: bahasa konkrit, butiran khusus; sokong pendapat dengan bukti.
Bentang maklumat secara **ringkas dan cekap** — Mesej ringkas menghormati masa dan meningkatkan peluang respons positif.
**Jelaskan jangkaan dan tanggungjawab** — Reka mesej untuk respons tertentu daripada audiens tertentu.
Tawarkan hujah dan cadangan yang **meyakinkan** — Tunjukkan dengan tepat bagaimana pembaca beruntung.

blocks.en: Effective = Factual, Concise, Clear on duties, Persuasive.
blocks.ms: Berkesan = Fakta, Ringkas, Jelas tugas, Memujuk.

en: **Provide practical information** that helps recipients act or understand a policy.
ms: **Beri maklumat mudah dilaksanakan** untuk membantu penerima bertindak atau memahami dasar.

en: Express ideas concisely, coherently and persuasively
ms: Menyatakan idea secara ringkas, koheren dan meyakinkan
Standard penulisan dan pertuturan berkualiti tinggi

blocks.en: **Professionalism** is the quality of performing at a high level and conducting oneself with purpose and pride. True professionals go beyond minimum expectations (more than putting in hours and collecting a paycheck) and commit to meaningful contributions.
blocks.ms: **Profesionalisme** ialah kualiti melaksanakan tugas pada tahap tinggi dan membawa diri dengan tujuan dan bangga. Profesional sebenar melampaui jangkaan minimum dan komited membuat sumbangan bermakna.

en: Striving to excel — Pros strive to excel; they keep promises, meet commitments, learn from mistakes and take responsibility for errors.
Being a team player — Pros contribute to a larger cause and make others around them better.
Demonstrating a sense of etiquette — Good etiquette is a sign of **respect**; respecting others is good for your career.
Making ethical decisions — Responsible pros avoid ethical lapses and weigh options carefully in ethical dilemmas.
ms: Berusaha untuk cemerlang — Profesional berusaha cemerlang; tepati janji, penuhi komitmen, belajar daripada kesilapan dan bertanggungjawab.
Pemain pasukan — Profesional menyumbang kepada matlamat lebih besar dan menjadikan orang lain lebih baik.
Menunjukkan adab/etiket — Etiket baik tanda **hormat**; menghormati orang baik untuk kerjaya.
Membuat keputusan beretika — Profesional bertanggungjawab elak kecuaian etika dan menimbang pilihan dengan teliti apabila berdepan dilema etika.

en: Excellent communication with people from **diverse backgrounds**
Effective and efficient use of communication technologies
ms: Menyatakan idea secara **ringkas, koheren dan meyakinkan**
Komunikasi baik dengan orang dari **latar belakang pelbagai**
Guna teknologi komunikasi dengan berkesan dan cekap
Standard penulisan dan pertuturan berkualiti tinggi

groups.en: What is important to your audience?
groups.ms: Apa yang penting kepada audiens anda?

en: If you don’t know your audience

blocks.en: Adopt an **audience-centred approach**: focus on the **“you” attitude**, use **emotional intelligence** and practise **business etiquette**.
blocks.ms: Guna **pendekatan berpusatkan audiens**: fokus kepada **sikap “you”**, guna **kecerdasan emosi** dan amalkan **etiket perniagaan**.

blocks.en: What is important to your audience?
blocks.ms: Apa yang penting kepada audiens anda?

blocks.en: Slide 13 (Figure 1.4 Formal Communication Network) is an image and has no text. See your textbook for the diagram.
blocks.ms: Slaid 13 (Rajah 1.4 Rangkaian Komunikasi Formal) ialah imej tanpa teks. Rujuk buku teks untuk rajah.

blocks.en: Defined by the relationships between job positions. Messages flow **upward** (lower to higher level), **downward** (higher to lower) and **horizontally** (between employees at the same or similar levels).
blocks.ms: Ditakrif oleh hubungan antara jawatan. Mesej mengalir **ke atas** (rendah ke tinggi), **ke bawah** (tinggi ke rendah) dan **mendatar** (antara pekerja pada tahap sama atau serupa).

en: If you don’t know your audience, project yourself into their position using common sense and imagination. This ability to relate to others’ needs is part of **emotional intelligence** (a combination of emotional and social skills).
**Etiquette** = the expected norms of behaviour in any particular situation. Executives expect your behaviour to protect the company’s reputation.
ms: Jika tidak kenal audiens, letakkan diri dalam posisi mereka dengan akal dan bayangan. Kebolehan ini sebahagian daripada **kecerdasan emosi** (gabungan kemahiran emosi dan sosial).
**Etiket** = norma tingkah laku yang dijangka dalam sesuatu situasi. Eksekutif mengharapkan tingkah laku anda melindungi nama baik syarikat.

blocks.en: The basic model shows a **sender** encoding a message, sending it through a **channel**, and a **receiver** decoding it and giving **feedback**. (Slide 16 is a figure: Figure 1.5.)
blocks.ms: Model asas menunjukkan **penghantar** mengekod mesej, menghantarnya melalui **saluran**, dan **penerima** menyahkod serta memberi **maklum balas**. (Slaid 16 ialah rajah: Rajah 1.5.)

blocks.en: Extra (not in slides): the step labels (sender, encode, channel, decode, receiver, feedback) are standard model wording from the textbook figure, not listed in the slide text.
blocks.ms: Extra (bukan dalam slaid): label langkah (sender, encode, channel, decode, receiver, feedback) ialah perkataan model standard dari rajah buku teks, tidak disenaraikan dalam teks slaid.

blocks.en: Even with the best intentions, communication can fail: messages get lost or ignored, or the receiver interprets them in ways the sender never imagined. The process is studied in two stages: the **basic communication model** (one sender, one receiver) and then the **social communication model** (many messages and participants).
blocks.ms: Walaupun niat baik, komunikasi boleh gagal: mesej hilang atau diabaikan, atau ditafsir cara yang tidak dijangka. Proses dikaji dalam dua peringkat: **model komunikasi asas** (satu penghantar, satu penerima) kemudian **model komunikasi sosial** (banyak mesej dan peserta).

blocks.en: The eight-step model is a simplified view of real communication. Minimising barriers and distractions is **everyone’s responsibility**.
blocks.ms: Model lapan langkah ialah gambaran ringkas. Meminimumkan halangan dan gangguan ialah **tanggungjawab semua orang**.

blocks.en: Within any communication environment, messages can be disrupted by barriers. Minimising barriers and distractions is **everyone’s responsibility**.
blocks.ms: Dalam mana-mana persekitaran komunikasi, mesej boleh terganggu oleh halangan. Meminimumkan halangan ialah **tanggungjawab semua orang**.

title.en: Inside the Mind of Your Audience

en: The recipient must be able to respond
ms: Penerima mesti mampu bertindak balas dan bermotivasi

en: Social media tools also bring communication challenges
ms: Alat media sosial juga membawa cabaran komunikasi

en: Consider audience expectations, ensure ease of use, emphasise familiarity, practise empathy, design for compatibility
ms: Pertimbang jangkaan audiens, mudah guna, tekankan keakraban, amalkan empati, reka untuk keserasian

en: Affected by perception, selective perception, cultural beliefs, personal beliefs, individual thinking styles
ms: Dipengaruhi tanggapan, tanggapan terpilih, kepercayaan budaya, kepercayaan peribadi, gaya pemikiran individu

en: Audience must remember the message, be able to respond as you wish, and be motivated to respond
ms: Audiens mesti ingat mesej, mampu bertindak balas seperti anda mahu, dan bermotivasi untuk bertindak balas

blocks.en: R-D-R: Receive, Decode, Respond. Shared experience helps understanding (Figure 1.6).
blocks.ms: R-D-R: Receive, Decode, Respond. Pengalaman bersama membantu kefahaman (Rajah 1.6).

blocks.en: Slides 21 and 23 are figures (Figure 1.6 shared experience, Figure 1.7 social communication model); their slide notes are included below. Slide 24 is a blank slide.
blocks.ms: Slaid 21 dan 23 ialah rajah (Rajah 1.6 pengalaman bersama, Rajah 1.7 model komunikasi sosial); nota slaid disertakan di bawah. Slaid 24 ialah slaid kosong.

blocks.en: To truly receive a message, the audience must **sense** it, **select** it, then **perceive** it as a message. Five ways to improve the odds:
blocks.ms: Untuk benar-benar menerima mesej, audiens mesti **mengesan**, **memilih**, kemudian **mentafsir**nya sebagai mesej. Lima cara menambah peluang:

en: **Expectations**: use the media/channels the audience expects (e.g. don’t switch meeting notices from email to blog without telling anyone).
**Ease of use**: if messages are hard to find, navigate or read, they won’t be seen.
**Familiarity**: familiar words, images and designs (e.g. “About Us” page).
**Empathy**: address the audience’s wants and needs, not yours.
**Compatibility**: verify technical compatibility (e.g. video software needed to view your site).
ms: **Jangkaan**: guna media/saluran yang dijangka (cth jangan tukar notis mesyuarat daripada e-mel ke blog tanpa memberitahu).
**Mudah guna**: jika sukar dicari, dilayari atau dibaca, ia tidak akan dilihat.
**Keakraban**: perkataan, imej dan reka bentuk yang biasa (cth halaman “About Us”).
**Empati**: tangani kehendak dan keperluan audiens, bukan anda.
**Keserasian**: pastikan keserasian teknikal (cth perisian video untuk melihat laman web).

en: Receivers often extract different meanings from those the sender encoded.
**Selective perception**: people ignore or distort information to fit preconceived notions (e.g. a business strategy ignoring evidence it is failing).
Language differences: “as soon as possible” could mean 10 seconds, 10 minutes or 10 days. Clarify expectations to remove ambiguity.
The **more shared experiences**, the more shared meaning (Figure 1.6).
Thinking styles: objective analysis/logic vs emotion/intuition lead to different interpretations.
ms: Penerima sering mengambil makna berbeza daripada yang dikodkan penghantar.
**Tanggapan terpilih**: orang abaikan atau putarbelit maklumat supaya sesuai tanggapan sedia ada.
Perbezaan bahasa: “secepat mungkin” boleh bermakna 10 saat, 10 minit atau 10 hari. Jelaskan jangkaan.
**Lebih banyak pengalaman bersama**, lebih banyak makna dikongsi (Rajah 1.6).
Gaya pemikiran: analisis objektif/logik berbanding emosi/gerak hati menghasilkan tafsiran berbeza.

en: **Sensory memory** captures data momentarily; what the recipient pays attention to moves to **short-term memory**.
Short-term information disappears unless moved to **long-term memory**: actively (memorising) or passively (connecting to something already stored).
Information must then be **retrieved** when needed. People remember things important to them, so be sensitive to audience wants and needs.
The recipient must be **able** to respond (understand your audience, Chapter 4) and **motivated** to respond (e.g. a record company may or may not offer your band a contract).
ms: **Memori deria** menangkap data seketika; apa yang diberi perhatian berpindah ke **memori jangka pendek**.
Maklumat jangka pendek hilang kecuali dipindahkan ke **jangka panjang**: secara aktif (menghafal) atau pasif (dikaitkan dengan yang sedia ada).
Maklumat perlu **dipanggil semula** apabila diperlukan. Orang ingat perkara penting kepada mereka.
Penerima mesti **mampu** bertindak balas dan **bermotivasi** (cth syarikat rakaman mungkin tidak menawarkan kontrak).

en: Interactive, conversational and usually **open to all** who wish to participate (contrast with the traditional publishing mindset).
Benefits: faster communication, lower costs, better access to expertise, higher employee satisfaction.
Social media tools also bring communication challenges.
ms: Dua hala, berbual dan biasanya **terbuka kepada semua** (berbeza dengan minda penerbitan tradisional).
Manfaat: komunikasi lebih pantas, kos rendah, akses kepakaran lebih baik, kepuasan pekerja tinggi.
Alat media sosial juga membawa cabaran komunikasi.

groups.ms: Cara mudah alih mengubah komunikasi perniagaan

en: Constant connectivity is a mixed blessing
Companies integrate mobile in communication platforms, banking and retail. Mobile can boost productivity, build closer customer/partner relationships and spur innovation (Figure 1.8).
Mobile connectivity resembles a **continuous stream of conversations** that never quite end; wearables would extend this (Figure 1.9).
Social media and mobile are parallel: both change the nature of communication, alter sender-receiver relationships, bring opportunities and challenges, and demand new skills.
ms: Syarikat menggabungkan mudah alih dalam platform komunikasi, perbankan dan runcit; meningkatkan produktiviti, hubungan pelanggan dan inovasi.
Sambungan mudah alih seperti **aliran perbualan berterusan**; peranti boleh pakai menambahnya.
Media sosial dan mudah alih selari: mengubah sifat komunikasi, hubungan penghantar-penerima, ada peluang dan cabaran, dan perlukan kemahiran baharu.

en: Globally, more than **80%** of Internet users access the web with a mobile device
Mobile is the **primary communication tool** for many professionals; a majority of executives **under 40** use mobile as their main tool
**Email** and **web browsing** are the most common non-voice uses of smartphones
More email messages are now opened on **mobile devices than on PCs**
Roughly **half** of U.S. consumers use mobile **exclusively** for online search
ms: Di seluruh dunia, lebih **80%** pengguna Internet akses web dengan peranti mudah alih
Mudah alih ialah **alat komunikasi utama** ramai profesional; majoriti eksekutif **bawah 40 tahun** guna mudah alih sebagai alat utama
**E-mel** dan **layari web** ialah kegunaan bukan suara paling biasa telefon pintar
Lebih banyak e-mel dibuka pada **peranti mudah alih berbanding PC**
Kira-kira **separuh** pengguna AS guna mudah alih **sepenuhnya** untuk carian dalam talian

blocks.ms: Cara mudah alih mengubah komunikasi perniagaan

ms: Keputusan dan penyelesaian masalah lebih pantas

en: Security and privacy concerns; sensory and cognitive extensions of the user
ms: Kebimbangan keselamatan dan privasi; lanjutan deria dan daya fikir pengguna

blocks.en: Slide 28 lists “Sensory and Cognitive Extensions of User” with the other challenges; the slides do not label each item as a challenge or opportunity, so the grouping above is a study aid.
blocks.ms: Slaid 28 menyenaraikan “Sensory and Cognitive Extensions of User” bersama cabaran lain; slaid tidak melabel setiap item sebagai cabaran atau peluang, jadi pengelompokan di atas ialah bantuan belajar.

en: **Constant connectivity** is a mixed blessing: blurs personal/professional boundaries but gives flexibility (e.g. telecommuting).
**Small displays** and awkward input make creating and consuming content harder (emails need different formatting, Chapter 6).
**Multitasking**: roughly half of mobile use happens while walking; attention is split and distractions are many.
**Grammar pressure**: texting puts pressure on standards of grammar, punctuation and writing.
**Sensory and cognitive extensions**: augmented reality, instant information access, location-aware content.
ms: **Sentiasa bersambung** berbaur: mengaburkan sempadan peribadi/kerja tetapi memberi fleksibiliti.
**Paparan kecil** dan input kekok menyukarkan penciptaan dan penggunaan kandungan.
**Multitugas**: kira-kira separuh penggunaan semasa berjalan; perhatian berpecah.
**Tekanan tatabahasa**: teks menekan standard tatabahasa dan penulisan.
**Lanjutan deria dan daya fikir**: realiti terimbuh, akses maklumat segera, kandungan sedar lokasi.

en: **BYOD**: employees want to use personal smartphones/tablets for company networks and files, but these lack rigorous security controls.
**Productivity and collaboration**: stay connected during gaps in the day or travel.
**Apps**: from research to presentations; companies can create custom apps with digital publishing tools.
**Faster decisions**: right information to the right people at the right time; tap expertise; better customer service; faster crisis communication.
**Engagement**: use cameras, accelerometers, compasses and GPS for more engaging experiences.
ms: **BYOD**: pekerja mahu guna telefon/tablet peribadi untuk rangkaian syarikat tetapi kawalan keselamatan lemah.
**Produktiviti dan kerjasama**: kekal bersambung semasa waktu terluang atau bermusafir.
**Aplikasi**: dari penyelidikan hingga pembentangan; syarikat boleh cipta apl khas.
**Keputusan lebih pantas**: maklumat betul kepada orang betul pada masa betul; akses kepakaran; perkhidmatan pelanggan; komunikasi krisis.
**Penglibatan**: guna kamera, pecutan, kompas dan GPS untuk pengalaman lebih menarik.

en: Implement controls on the messages you receive
Face-to-face or phone can limit miscommunication
Use technology as an aid, not a replacement
Show people who you really are
ms: Bersemuka atau telefon boleh kurangkan salah faham
Guna teknologi sebagai bantuan, bukan pengganti

en: Businesses rely heavily on technology; poorly designed or inappropriate use hinders more than it helps.

To communicate effectively: keep technology in perspective, **guard against information overload and information addiction**, use tools productively, and frequently disengage to **communicate in person**.
ms: Perniagaan bergantung kuat kepada teknologi; reka bentuk buruk atau penggunaan tidak sesuai menghalang.
Untuk berkesan: letak teknologi dalam sudut pandangan, **elak beban dan ketagihan maklumat**, guna secara berhasil, dan kerap bersemuka.

en: **Keep technology in perspective** — Don’t rely too much on technology or let it overwhelm the communication process.
**Guard against information overload** — You control the number and types of messages you receive; filter high-priority messages, be wary of too many Twitter streams.

**Use technological tools productively** — Basic technical competence is needed. Social media can waste employee time; inappropriate web use can expose employers to **sexual harassment lawsuits**; managers must guide productive use.
**Reconnect with people** — Communication is still about people connecting with people; step out from behind the technology to learn about colleagues and let them learn about you.
ms: **Letakkan teknologi dalam sudut pandangan** — Jangan terlalu bergantung kepada teknologi.
**Elak beban maklumat berlebihan** — Anda kawal jenis dan bilangan mesej; tapis mesej keutamaan, berhati-hati dengan terlalu banyak aliran.
**Guna alat teknologi secara berhasil** — Perlu kecekapan teknikal asas. Media sosial membazir masa; penggunaan web tidak sesuai boleh membawa **saman gangguan seksual**; pengurus perlu membimbing.
**Berhubung semula dengan orang** — Komunikasi tetap tentang manusia; keluar dari belakang teknologi untuk mengenali rakan sekerja.

en: Implement controls on the messages you receive

Avoid sending unnecessary messages — As a sender, don’t send unnecessary messages; signal non-urgent messages; use “urgent” only when truly needed (overuse leads to annoyance and anxiety, not action).
ms: Elak hantar mesej tidak perlu — Sebagai penghantar, jangan hantar mesej tidak perlu; tanda mesej tidak segera; guna “urgent” hanya jika benar-benar perlu.

en: Face-to-face or phone can limit miscommunication
Use technology as an **aid, not a replacement**
Show people who you really are
ms: Bersemuka atau telefon boleh kurangkan salah faham

blocks.en: The four guideline names are taken from the slide headings (Keeping Technology in Perspective, Guarding Against Information Overload, Using Technological Tools Productively, Reconnecting With People).
blocks.ms: Empat nama garis panduan diambil daripada tajuk slaid.

en: Is not deceptive in any way
ms: Tidak mengelirukan dalam apa cara pun

en: Failing to respect privacy or security
Choosing among alternatives that are not clear-cut
ms: Memilih antara pilihan lain yang tidak jelas
Dasar dan struktur sesuai (cth kod etika, audit etika)

en: Have you defined the situation fairly and accurately?
What is your intention in communicating this message?
Will your assumptions change over time
ms: Adakah anda mentakrif situasi secara adil dan tepat?
Apakah niat anda menyampaikan mesej ini?
Adakah andaian anda berubah dari masa ke masa?

groups.en: Six questions for ethical choices (slide 39 notes)
groups.ms: Enam soalan untuk pilihan beretika (nota slaid 39)

en: **Ethics** = accepted principles of conduct that govern behaviour in a society. Communication is the public face of a company, so it faces scrutiny from regulators, legislators, investors, consumer/environmental groups and labour organisations.
**Transparency** = openness; giving all participants the information they need to process messages accurately. Audiences deserve to know when they are being marketed to and who is behind messages.
**Stealth marketing**: recruiting people to promote products to friends for free samples/rewards without disclosing it. Critics, including the US **FTC**, say it is deceptive.

**Ethical dilemma**: alternatives are not clear-cut; two conflicting alternatives may both be ethical, or lie in a grey area. Example: employees want higher wages while investors want low costs; both have a valid position.
**Ethical lapse**: a clearly unethical choice. Example: promising a client a completion date you know you can’t meet, even to save your career or company.
The three elements (individuals, leadership, policies) must work in **harmony**. If executives flout guidelines, employees may conclude guidelines are meaningless.
If in doubt about the legality of a message, ask the **legal department**.
ms: **Etika** = prinsip tingkah laku yang diterima dalam masyarakat. Komunikasi ialah wajah awam syarikat, justeru diteliti oleh pengawal selia, penggubal undang-undang, pelabur dan kumpulan lain.
**Ketelusan** = keterbukaan; memberi semua pihak maklumat untuk memproses mesej dengan tepat.
**Pemasaran senyap (stealth)**: merekrut orang mempromosi produk kepada rakan tanpa mendedahkan. Pengkritik termasuk **FTC** AS menganggapnya menipu.
**Dilema etika**: pilihan lain tidak jelas; dua pilihan bercanggah mungkin kedua-duanya beretika. Contoh: pekerja mahu gaji tinggi, pelabur mahu kos rendah.
**Kecuaian etika**: pilihan jelas tidak beretika. Contoh: berjanji tarikh siap yang anda tahu tidak boleh dipenuhi.
Tiga elemen mesti berfungsi **harmoni**. Jika eksekutif melanggar garis panduan, pekerja anggap ia tidak bermakna.
Jika ragu tentang kesahan undang-undang mesej, tanya **jabatan undang-undang**.

en: Failing to respect privacy or security
Choosing among alternatives that are **not clear-cut**
ms: Memilih antara pilihan lain yang **tidak jelas**

en: **Appropriate policies and structures** (e.g. code of ethics, ethics audits) — A **code of ethics** is part of a larger programme of training and channels to ask questions or report issues; **ethics audits** monitor progress and weaknesses.
ms: **Dasar dan struktur sesuai** (cth kod etika, audit etika) — Sebahagian program latihan dan saluran bertanya/melapor; **audit etika** memantau kemajuan dan kelemahan.

en: Have you defined the situation fairly and accurately?

What impact will it have on those who receive it or are affected?

q.en: Scenario: Nadia leads a six-member software team working partly from home. She posts important instructions in a group chat late at night and expects instant replies. Two members, Aiman and Farah, disagree on the project direction, while the rest stay quiet and agree with the loudest member, Hakim. Her team meeting (20 people, no agenda) is dominated by Hakim, people check their phones and no minutes are kept. Her client report has long dense paragraphs, vague phrases and spelling mistakes in the client’s name. Her 30-slide presentation is full of small-font bullets and she hands out the slides at the start. The client says the proposal is unclear. ANALYSE the communication problems and give your OPINION on what Nadia should do (use Chapters 1, 2, 6 and 17).
q.ms: Senario: Nadia mengetuai pasukan perisian enam orang yang separuh bekerja dari rumah. Dia hantar arahan penting dalam chat kumpulan lewat malam dan mengharap balasan segera. Aiman dan Farah berbeza pendapat, yang lain senyap dan ikut Hakim. Mesyuarat (20 orang, tiada agenda) dikuasai Hakim, orang menyemak telefon dan tiada minit. Laporan klien padat, kabur dan ada silap ejaan nama klien. 30 slaid penuh bullet kecil dan slaid diedar di awal. Klien kata cadangan tidak jelas. ANALISIS masalah komunikasi dan beri PENDAPAT anda (guna Bab 1, 2, 6 dan 17).

en: Late-night messages and instant-reply expectation: mobile constant connectivity blurs boundaries; respect time boundaries; mark urgent only when truly urgent (3)
Groupthink and Hakim’s controlling role; silent members; lack of open and honest communication; encourage participation (3)
Unresolved conflict between Aiman and Farah: lack of proactive behaviour; apply openness, research, flexibility, fair play, alliance (3)
Meeting: 20 people (more than 10–12), no agenda, device misuse, no minutes; invite only those needed, agenda, rules, minutes (4)
Report: weak revision of content/organisation/tone, vague hedging, dense paragraphs, no proofreading of names; use headings, lists, short paragraphs, multiple proofreading passes (4)
Slides: death by PowerPoint, slideument, one idea per slide, 4–5 lines, key visual, detail in handout; handout timing risk (4)
Link to professionalism and audiences equating writing quality with thinking quality (1)
Clear, justified OPINION with priority of actions and cause-effect reasoning (3)
ms: Mesej lewat malam dan jangkaan balasan segera: sentiasa bersambung mengaburkan sempadan; hormati masa; “urgent” hanya jika benar-benar perlu (3)
Groupthink dan peranan controlling Hakim; ahli senyap; kurang komunikasi terbuka; galakkan penyertaan (3)
Konflik Aiman dan Farah tidak diselesaikan: tiada tindakan bertindak awal; guna keterbukaan, kajian, fleksibiliti, adil, pakatan (3)
Mesyuarat: 20 orang (lebih 10–12), tiada agenda, penyalahgunaan peranti, tiada minit; jemput yang perlu, agenda, peraturan, minit (4)
Laporan: semakan lemah kandungan/organisasi/nada, hedging, perenggan padat, tiada pruf nama; guna tajuk, senarai, perenggan pendek, pelbagai pusingan pruf (4)
Slaid: death by PowerPoint, slideument, satu idea, 4–5 baris, visual utama, butiran dalam handout; risiko masa edar handout (4)
Kaitkan dengan profesionalisme dan tanggapan audiens: kualiti penulisan = kualiti pemikiran (1)
PENDAPAT jelas dengan alasan, keutamaan tindakan dan sebab-akibat (3)

q.en: Analyse why a company with a strong code of ethics may still experience ethical lapses in its business communication, and give your opinion on how it can reduce them.
q.ms: Analisis mengapa syarikat dengan kod etika kukuh masih mengalami kecuaian etika dalam komunikasi perniagaannya, dan beri pendapat bagaimana ia boleh dikurangkan.

en: Three elements must work in harmony: individuals, leadership, policies and structures (2)
If executives flout guidelines, employees see them as meaningless and copy them (2)
Pressure to produce results or justify decisions makes unethical communication tempting, e.g. promising a date you can’t meet (2)
Code must be backed by training, channels to ask or report, and ethics audits (2)
Opinion with justification, e.g. leadership example, the six ethical questions (2)
ms: Tiga elemen mesti harmoni: individu, kepimpinan, dasar dan struktur (2)
Jika eksekutif melanggar garis panduan, pekerja anggap tidak bermakna dan meniru (2)
Tekanan hasil atau mewajarkan keputusan menjadikan komunikasi tidak beretika menggoda, cth janji tarikh yang tidak boleh dipenuhi (2)
Kod perlu disokong latihan, saluran bertanya/melapor dan audit etika (2)
Pendapat dengan alasan, cth teladan kepimpinan, enam soalan etika (2)
